messages:
Priya: heads-up — received an escalated ticket from ACME: customers hitting 504s and high p95 latency on /v1/generate since ~20:15 UTC. They see bulk failures from multiple regions. Jordan (CS): customer reports 40% of requests failing with 504, started ~20:10 and persisted ~30–40m. They provided request ids in the ticket.
Sam: digging into gateway logs now, paging traces. Any quick mitigations we can do for the customer?
Jordan (CS): customer asked for ETA and whether we can route them to a warm fallback model or increase retries. They’re seeing billing spikes too in reports.
Alex: initial signal — a spike of auth-proxy latency around 20:08. Many requests to our auth service timed out waiting on KMS token refresh (50–2000ms, tail heavy). Gateway then tripped circuit for backend RPCs -> 504s.
Marta: confirming — KV-cache miss rate jumped at same time which increased token refresh frequency. That amplified auth traffic to KMS.
Kai: ops-bot attach: deploy and autoscaler logs show auth-proxy pods hit file-descriptor spikes and some 502/503 before OOM restarts.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-337333 — severity: P1. Runbook: /runbooks/saas/hosted-timeouts. Pager duty notified.
Sam: repro attempt: curl to /v1/generate with customer's token reproduced ~600ms auth step locally (should be <50ms). Attaching sample headers and trace ids: trace=337333-a1b2.
Priya: mitigation applied: scaled auth-proxy replicas x3 and temporarily disabled strict token refresh (allow reuse for 10m). Also enabled a circuit breaker delay on gateway to reduce fanout. Not ideal but reduced error rate.
Jordan (CS): customer confirmed fewer 504s after mitigation, now down to ~3% from 40%. They asked for root cause and next steps.
Marta: root-cause hypothesis: a sudden KV cache eviction (likely from a maintenance flurry in eu-west pool) caused many sessions to miss local creds, triggering mass KMS refreshes which pushed auth-proxy latency up -> backend RPC timeouts -> gateway 504. KMS also responded with a short-lived throttling spike.
Alex: logs show spike correlates with a node pool rolling update at 20:05 in eu-west that coincided with a batch job that forced a cache eviction.
Kai: followups we should do now: 1) restore stable cache warmup policy and pin critical nodes; 2) add backoff in auth-proxy for KMS errors and expose counters; 3) add alert for KV miss surge and KMS latency >200ms; 4) postmortem and customer comms draft.
Sam: creating a quick checklist for on-call handoff:
```
- capture list of affected customers + request ids
- export gateway traces for 20:00–20:50
- collect auth-proxy logs & metrics, KMS API latencies
- confirm scaling events and rollouts
- snapshot billing spikes for customer view
```
Priya: I’ve uploaded traces to the incident folder and granted CS a view link. Also opened a support ticket with KMS provider to confirm if they reported a transient throttle.
Jordan (CS): thanks — I’ll draft an external comm: explain short-term mitigation, ETA for permanent fix, and offer an SLA credit if they want. Will share draft for review.
Marta: technical action items (assignments):
- Marta: implement cache-warmup and eviction guard (ETA 72h)
- Alex: add KMS backoff & metrics to auth-proxy (ETA 48h)
- Sam: gateway fallback tuning + add p95/p999 alert (ETA 48h)
- Kai: autoscaler/file-descriptor mitigations and pod lifecycle changes (ETA 24h)
- Priya: coordinate KMS vendor follow-up and internal doc (ETA 24h)
Priya: short-term deploys: I’ll push the auth-proxy backoff PR to staging, request a canary once Alex’s change lands.
Alex: note — we should add a test in our integration suite that simulates KMS latency spikes and validates gateway fallbacks. Adding that to backlog.
Jordan (CS): customer comm draft posted to incident doc, asking to include timeline and a pointer to toggles they can use (retry/backoff from SDK).
Kai: oncall handoff at 04:00 UTC. I’ll monitor the KMS vendor reply and ensure alerts are quiet.
Sam: closing loop — ticket updated, mitigation notes added. Reprioritizing tasks in next sprint to prevent recurrence.
Priya: thanks everyone. We’ll run a short postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC — invite sent.
Jordan (CS): customer accepted mitigation and asked for weekly updates until fixes are in prod. I’ll set cadence. :thumbsup:
